method: Dispatch edge counts were normalized by the number of protein-coding genes on each chromosome (Ensembl GRCh38 counts). The outbound/inbound ratio was recomputed as (outbound_edges/genes) / (inbound_edges/genes).
conclusion: chr19 remains the dominant outbound hub after normalizing for gene density. The normalized ratio (1.60) is higher than the raw ratio (1.55), and the gap to the second-ranked chromosome increases from 7.4% to 9.2%. chr19's hub status is not a consequence of higher gene density; per-gene outbound traffic is genuinely higher than any other chromosome.
